title: Split-family strictification with a compatible coherent map
statement:
Use categories in the sense of [def-nagata-category] and universes of [def-weil-size-convention], enlarged to contain all the families below. Let $J$ be a small category. A normalized covariant category-valued pseudofunctor $P$ assigns a category $P(j)$ to each object, a functor $P(a):P(j)\to P(k)$ to each $a:j\to k$, and natural isomorphisms $\mu_{b,a}:P(b)P(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}P(ba)$. Require $P(1)=1$, identity comparisons when either arrow is an identity, and
$$\mu_{c,ba}\circ P(c)(\mu_{b,a})=\mu_{cb,a}\circ(\mu_{c,b}P(a)).$$
Let $H:J\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be a strict functor. Suppose functors $\alpha_j:H(j)\to P(j)$ have natural isomorphisms $\theta_a:P(a)\alpha_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\alpha_k H(a)$, identity at identities, satisfying
$$\theta_{ba}\circ(\mu_{b,a}\alpha_j)=(\theta_b H(a))\circ P(b)(\theta_a).$$
Here a strict functor preserves identities and composition by equality, and an equivalence of categories is a functor with a quasi-inverse and inverse natural isomorphisms.

Define $\widetilde P(j)$ to have objects families $X_a\in P(k)$ for every arrow $a:j\to k$, with isomorphisms $\gamma_{b,a}:P(b)X_a\xrightarrow{\sim}X_{ba}$ for each composable $b$, satisfying $\gamma_{1,a}=1$ and
$$\gamma_{c,ba}\circ P(c)(\gamma_{b,a})=\gamma_{cb,a}\circ\mu_{c,b}(X_a).$$
A morphism $X\to Y$ is a family $t_a:X_a\to Y_a$ with $t_{ba}\gamma^X_{b,a}=\gamma^Y_{b,a}P(b)(t_a)$. Evaluation $E_j(X)=X_{1_j}$ is an equivalence of categories, and reindexing $X_a\mapsto X_{aa_0}$ along $a_0:j\to j_1$ makes $\widetilde P$ a strict functor on $J$. There are coherent natural isomorphisms $\kappa_a:P(a)E_j\xrightarrow{\sim}E_k\widetilde P(a)$ with components $\gamma_{a,1_j}$. The formulas
$$\widetilde\alpha_j(z)_a=\alpha_k(H(a)z),\qquad \gamma_{b,a}=\theta_b(H(a)z)$$
(and the same formula on morphisms) define a strictly natural transformation $\widetilde\alpha:H\to\widetilde P$, with $E_j\widetilde\alpha_j=\alpha_j$; its comparison along $a$ under $\kappa_a$ is $\theta_a$.

More precisely, let $v:I\to J$ be a functor for which $P\circ v$ is strict, all its $\mu$ are identities, and $\alpha\circ v$ is strictly natural with all its $\theta$ identities. There is a strict functor $K:I\to\mathsf{Cat}$, a natural transformation $H\circ v\to K$, and strictly natural functors
$$\widetilde P\circ v\longleftarrow K\longrightarrow P\circ v$$
which are objectwise equivalences. Their composites on $H\circ v$ are respectively $\widetilde\alpha\circ v$ and $\alpha\circ v$. Thus the comparison also holds for diagrams equipped with these specified maps, not only object by object.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, lines 7747-7802: splitting a fibred category, dualized for covariant diagrams. The statement specifies the split-family model and compatibility with a given coherent map and strict restrictions. Compare Toën, The homotopy theory of dg-categories and derived Morita theory, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, Section 4, printed pp. 21-22, the standard rectification paragraph immediately before Sublemma 4.6. That PDF was read online and is absent locally.

mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: inspected StrictPseudofunctor.lean:12-21,40-85,105-165 and Coherence.lean:13-35. StrictPseudofunctor constructors assume strict composition data already; toFunctor forgets a supplied strict pseudofunctor; Functor.toPseudoFunctor converts an already strict diagram in the opposite direction. Coherence proves local thinness of a free bicategory. None replaces an arbitrary Cat-valued pseudofunctor by a strict diagram or gives the comparison compatible with a specified coherent map. Two semantic phrasings, Loogle, LeanSearch and source grep found no match.
